title: ASSISTANCE TO COASTAL FISHERMEN
body_text:
The annual fish production in the country has registered a steady increase from 147.25 lakh tonnes in 2020–21 to 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024–25. The year-wise fish production during the period from 2020–21 to 2024–25 is as follows:
Sl No Year Fish production (in lakh tonnes) 1 2020-21 147.25 2 2021-22 162.48 3 2022-23 175.45 4 2023-24 183.93 5 2024-25 197.75
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing the following schemes/ programmes for holistic development of fisheries including welfare of coastal fishermen in the country.
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY): The Department has been implementing PMMSY from Financial Year 2020-21 with an estimated investment of Rs.20,750 crore for holistic development of fisheries sector including welfare of fishers and fish farmers in the country.
Fisheries & Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF): In order to address the infrastructure requirement for fisheries sector, FIDF was launched in the year 2018-19 with a total funds size of Rs 7522.48 crore. FIDF provides concessional finance to the Eligible Entities (EEs), including State Governments/Union Territories for development of identified fisheries infrastructure facilities. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India provides interest subvention up to 3% per annum for the repayment period of 12 years inclusive of moratorium of 2 years for providing the concessional finance by the Nodal Loaning Entities (NLEs) at the interest rate not lower than 5% per annum.
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (PMMKSSY): To make the fisheries sector resilient and incentivize adoption of efficiencies in fisheries value chain, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has been implementing a Central Sector Sub-scheme "Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (PMMKSSY)" a sub-scheme under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with an investment of Rs. 6000 crore. PMMKSSY aims at formalization of the fisheries sector, incentivizing the aquaculture insurance, fisheries micro and small enterprises value chain efficiency, adoption of safety and quality system for safe fish production etc. Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish farmers: Additionally, the Government of India with effect from the financial year 2018-19 has extended the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish famers to help them to meet their working capital requirements.
The development of fishing harbours, fish landing centres and fisheries infrastructure facilities is one of the important areas envisaged and are supported under the PMMSY and FIDF. Under the PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last five years has approved 28 Fishing Harbour development/ modernization projects, 25 Fish Landing Centre projects, and 23 dredging projects at a total approved cost of Rs. 3,741.89 crore. Under FIDF, t he Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last five years has approved another 94 fishing harbours and fish landing centres at a total of cost of Rs.4916.46 crore and its projects cost restricted for interest subvention at Rs.3651.19 crore. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India under PMMSY and FIDF has also approved proposals amounting to Rs 2,797 crore for development of cold chain and marketing facilities in the country including coastal areas. The key activities approved includes; 775 cold storages and ice plants, 28,489 units of fish transportation facilities such as 13,718 motorcycles with ice boxes, 8,527 bicycles with ice boxes, 4,257 auto rickshaws, 1,577 insulated trucks and 410 refrigerated trucks, 1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, 117 retail fish markets, 24 wholesale fish markets in all the States and Union Territories.
The State-wise details of projects approved, funds released and number of beneficiaries under PMMSY during the FY 2020-21 to FY 2025-26 are furnished at Annexure.

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying informed the Lok Sabha that India's annual fish production rose from 147.25 lakh tonnes in 2020-21 to 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024-25. It detailed key schemes for coastal fishermen's welfare and infrastructure development — PMMSY, FIDF, PMMKSSY, and Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility for fishers — along with approved fishing harbour, landing centre, dredging, cold chain and marketing projects, and state-wise funding and beneficiary data under PMMSY from 2020-21 to 2025-26.
enrichment.context: Fisheries is a significant contributor to India's agricultural GDP and rural livelihoods, employing over 28 million people and making India the second-largest fish producer and largest shrimp exporter globally. The sector has been prioritized under the 'Blue Revolution' vision, with the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), launched in 2020 as a flagship scheme (with an outlay of Rs. 20,050 crore originally, cited here as Rs. 20,750 crore) aiming to double fish exports and enhance productivity, post-harvest infrastructure, and value chains. The Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), launched in 2018-19, complements PMMSY by offering concessional finance for infrastructure like fishing harbours and cold storage through Nodal Loaning Entities. The newer PMMKSSY sub-scheme focuses on formalizing the informal fisheries sector, promoting insurance and value-chain efficiency, echoing the broader push toward financial inclusion and risk mitigation seen in agriculture (e.g., PM Fasal Bima Yojana). Extension of Kisan Credit Card to fishers since 2018-19 mirrors similar credit-access reforms for farmers, addressing working capital needs of a traditionally credit-starved community. Collectively, these measures reflect India's Blue Economy policy framework, which links coastal community welfare, food security, and export competitiveness, and is periodically discussed in Parliament through such replies, making it a recurring theme in current affairs relevant to governance and economic development questions.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) has been implemented by the Department of Fisheries since which financial year?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, PMMSY has been implemented from Financial Year 2020-21 with an estimated investment of Rs. 20,750 crore.

prelims_questions.question: Under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), the Department of Fisheries provides interest subvention of up to what percentage per annum?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that the Department of Fisheries provides interest subvention up to 3% per annum for the repayment period of 12 years, including a 2-year moratorium.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of schemes like PMMSY and FIDF in transforming India's fisheries sector. Evaluate their impact on coastal fishermen's welfare and infrastructure development.
